conditions.sig: no Previous-version block with docs.oasis-open.org URLs found on the HTML cover
conditions.condition: A stage past 01 cites its previous stage on the HTML cover
conditions.pulls: the URLs in the cover's Previous-version block
conditions.compares_to: at least one docs.oasis-open.org URL required when the revision number exceeds 01

conditions.sig: the HTML was rendered from a different revision
conditions.condition: The markdown front-matter date appears in the HTML
conditions.pulls: the document date heading from the markdown
conditions.compares_to: the rendered HTML text (absence means the HTML came from a different revision)

conditions.condition: The copyright year matches the document date year
conditions.pulls: the year in the OASIS copyright line
conditions.compares_to: the year of the front-matter document date

conditions.sig: must be produced by Microsoft Word
conditions.condition: A DOCX-native render was produced by Microsoft Word
conditions.pulls: the HTML Generator meta content
conditions.compares_to: must contain 'Microsoft Word' (a LibreOffice render differs in kind from the TC's precedent)

conditions.sig: browsers that ignore VML show nothing
conditions.condition: Every VML image has an <![if !vml]> img fallback
conditions.pulls: the counts of v:imagedata elements and vml-fallback img tags
conditions.compares_to: fallback count must cover VML count (the invisible-cover-logo class)

conditions.sig: which is not in the package; it 404s
conditions.condition: Every relative src/href the HTML references is included in the package
conditions.pulls: each package-relative src/href in the HTML (attribute values flattened across Word line wraps)
conditions.compares_to: the package file tree; a missing target 404s on publication

conditions.sig: Conformance section is a buried subsection
conditions.condition: At least one Conformance heading is a genuine top-level numbered section (not nested deeper than the document's modal top-level depth, and not under an Annex/Appendix ancestor)
conditions.pulls: every heading's nesting level, leading number prefix, and Annex/Appendix ancestor chain (markdown ATX headings, or rendered HTML h1-h6 on the DOCX-native track), with code-block content stripped first
conditions.compares_to: handbook-Conformance.txt: 'a separate, top-level numbered section of the work product (not a subsection buried elsewhere)'; BLOCKER at cs/os (WARN at wd/csd, or when the modal-depth signal itself is low-confidence)

conditions.condition: Each conformance profile scope yields at least one extracted clause identifier
conditions.pulls: numbered sub-headings and paragraph-leading 'Clause N'/bracketed target-id labels within the Conformance section span, scoped per named profile
conditions.compares_to: handbook-WPQualityRequirements.txt: 'a set of numbered conformance clauses to which any implementation must adhere'; BLOCKER at cs/os, WARN at wd/csd; an empty Conformance section is reported at either tier

conditions.condition: No clause identifier repeats within the same profile scope
conditions.pulls: the extracted clause-identifier set, scoped per named conformance profile (Core/Extended-style sub-headings matching 'Profile'/'Level')
conditions.compares_to: handbook-Conformance.txt: 'individually numbered conformance clauses ... so that implementers and Statements of Use can cite specific clauses by number'; BLOCKER at cs/os, WARN at wd/csd

conditions.condition: Every (profile, clause number) pair in the previous stage is still present in this stage (append-only extension is fine; removal/renumbering, including a whole profile silently disappearing, is flagged)
conditions.pulls: the ((profile, clause number) -> content hash) map extracted from the resolvable previous-stage artifact, diffed against this stage's map
conditions.compares_to: handbook-WPQualityRequirements.txt 'Key principles': 'Clause numbering must be unique and stable across revisions'. Guidelines-sourced (recommended, not mandatory) so WARN-tier informational, never BLOCKER, and never fired for the CS->OS transition (that gets the zero-tolerance override instead)

conditions.condition: A (profile, clause number) pair missing from this stage does not reappear under a DIFFERENT number in the same profile with the same content (a disguised renumber-via-delete-and-re-add)
conditions.pulls: content-hash collisions between a previous-stage clause and any current-stage clause, scoped within the same profile
conditions.compares_to: the same Guidelines stability principle as 'removed/renumbered'; WARN-tier informational

conditions.sig: OS conformance clause numbering differs from approved CS
conditions.condition: At the CS->OS transition, the current (profile, clause id) key set is a byte-for-byte match to the approved-CS key set, scoped per profile, so a whole profile silently dropped while a surviving profile happens to reuse its bare clause numbers is still caught
conditions.pulls: the (profile, clause-identifier) sets extracted from the OS package and from the artifact named by its Previous-stage URI (verified to be the approved CS by stage token), each parsed with the extractor matching that artifact's own format (markdown or rendered HTML)
conditions.compares_to: handbook-Conformance.txt 'OASIS Standard os': 'Conformance clauses are preserved unchanged from the approved Committee Specification' (TC Process 2.9): zero tolerance, always BLOCKER

conditions.sig: OS conformance clause wording differs from approved CS under a stable number
conditions.condition: A clause whose (profile, number) key is unchanged at CS->OS is flagged for manual confirmation when its content hash changed
conditions.pulls: content-hash comparison, per (profile, clause number) key, between the approved CS and the OS package, restricted to keys present in both sets
conditions.compares_to: handbook-WPQualityRequirements.txt 'Allowed changes during publication': coordinated non-material changes are permitted (TC Process 2.2.4); not itself a zero-tolerance failure, so WARN/manual-review, never an automatic BLOCKER

conditions.condition: At the CS->OS transition, the approved-CS baseline artifact must be resolvable to verify clause-set preservation at all
conditions.pulls: the resolution outcome (local sibling stage directory, then network fetch) of the Previous-stage URI naming the approved CS
conditions.compares_to: TC Process 2.9's preservation obligation cannot be verified for a Standards Track OS approval if the CS baseline is unreachable, so it is elevated to BLOCKER rather than reported as a silent WARN

conditions.sig: Stability not verified - previous stage unavailable
conditions.condition: A general (non-CS->OS) stability diff that could not resolve its previous-stage artifact says so in the report
conditions.pulls: the resolution outcome of the Previous-stage URI
conditions.compares_to: the general stability check is WARN-tier informational; an unresolvable prior artifact (first publication is a separate, silent no-op) still surfaces the gap as a WARN

conditions.sig: is not labeled Normative References / Informative References
conditions.condition: A bare 'References' heading carrying 2+ direct reference entries is split into separately labeled Normative/Informative child headings (or is too small a sample, 0 or 1 entries, to judge)
conditions.pulls: H1-H3 headings normalizing to 'references' plus the distinct reference-entry IDs found directly in that heading's own span (before its first immediate-child heading)
conditions.compares_to: handbook-WPQualityChecklist.txt editorial quality checklist bullet: 'normative references listed separately from informative references' (WARN: staff-maintained best-practice checklist, not a TC Process must/shall clause)

conditions.sig: is listed under both Normative References and
conditions.condition: No reference-entry ID appears under both a Normative References heading and an Informative References heading anywhere in the document
conditions.pulls: the set of reference-entry IDs found in the span of every 'normative references'-classified heading, and the same for every 'informative references'-classified heading
conditions.compares_to: the two ID sets must not intersect; a shared ID is a labeling inconsistency or editorial duplication (handbook-WPQualityChecklist.txt same checklist bullet)

conditions.sig: the Handbook classifies Examples as non-normative content
conditions.condition: Every Examples/Illustrative-Examples/Sample-<noun> heading carries a structural content-type label (heading suffix, first-sentence lead/predicate, labeled ancestor heading, or document-wide blanket statement)
conditions.pulls: markdown ATX/setext headings (or, DOCX-native track, rendered HTML h1-h6 elements via an HTMLParser walk, entities decoded), in document order, each with its heading text, nesting level, and the first sentence of the body block immediately following it
conditions.compares_to: handbook-Conformance.txt 'Normative versus non-normative content': Examples content is classified non-normative and 'should be clearly labelled'

conditions.condition: Previous-stage URL stage token is not a retired abbreviation
conditions.pulls: the stage-abbreviation token extracted from the Previous-stage URL's directory segment and/or filename stem
conditions.compares_to: retired token set (csprd, cnprd, cos, csdpr, cndpr) per Naming Directives v1.7; WARN with a legacy-URI verification caveat since a pre-2024 Previous-stage URI may permanently retain a retired token (naming-directives.txt 6.3 Resource Permanence)

conditions.condition: Previous-stage URL stage token matches the document's own current csd/cnd stage abbreviation or the track's approved-stage counterpart
conditions.pulls: the stage-abbreviation token extracted from the Previous-stage URL's directory segment and/or filename stem
conditions.compares_to: the document's own current stage token, or the track's approved-stage set (csd: cs/os/errata; cnd: cn) when the block links a previous VERSION at its own approved stage (handbook-PublicReviews.txt: the cover page URIs 'should all reflect the csd stage abbreviation')

conditions.condition: Latest-stage URL's filename embeds no stage-abbreviation/revision token at all
conditions.pulls: the filename-stem-position stage-abbreviation token (if any) extracted from the Latest-stage URL
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt 6.2: the Latest-stage locator URI 'does not contain the path component [stage-abbrev][revisionNumber] or stage identifier in the filename', an absolute prohibition independent of whether the token matches the current stage

conditions.sig: does not incorporate a Version identifier
conditions.condition: The rendered cover-page title incorporates the package's own Version identifier
conditions.pulls: the resolved cover-page title text (HTML <title>/<h1> on the markdown track, the MsoTitle-styled or first non-empty non-logo cover paragraph on the DOCX-native track)
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt 5.1: 'A Version identifier must also be incorporated into a Work Product name/title'

conditions.sig: cites a different Version than the package's own Version identifier
conditions.condition: The Version cited in the title agrees with the package's own Version identifier
conditions.pulls: the numeric run of the rightmost 'Version <n>' token in the resolved title
conditions.compares_to: the package's own Version identifier (the version directory segment, with a leading 'v' stripped per naming-directives.txt Section 4's [version-id] grammar)

conditions.sig: Version composition does not follow the required
conditions.condition: The title's Version token is composed as '<name/identifier> Version <number>' with no forbidden punctuation before it and only a sanctioned continuation after it (a '. Part N: <part title>' suffix; on a package whose own stage directory or immediate parent is named errataNN, also an 'Errata NN' or 'Plus Errata NN' suffix whose number matches the package's own errata number, per naming-directives.txt Section 4's separate Errata construction)
conditions.pulls: the characters immediately preceding and following the rightmost 'Version <n>' token in the resolved title, the stage token's track classification, and the package's own Errata number derived from its stage directory layout
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt Section 7: MUST for Standards Track (csd/cs/os/errata) -> BLOCKER; SHOULD for Non-Standards Track (cnd/cn) -> WARN with the 'reasonable grounds for alternate constructions' exception; WARN also for any stage token outside the six Section-5.2-enumerated tokens (track unresolved, no corpus citation, never escalated to BLOCKER on an uncited classification)

conditions.condition: The Work Product title (the <h1> identified by _h1_title_match_info's 'exact' or 'singular-related-fallback' classification) does not begin with the word 'OASIS'
conditions.pulls: the <h1> text identified by _h1_title_match_info: either the single <h1> exactly matching the rendered <title> text (the same match check_html's own D1 lint uses for its duplicate-title finding), or, when no exact match exists, the document's sole <h1> when it shares a prefix relationship with <title> (e.g. a trailing brand suffix on <title> alone), flagged lower-confidence in that case
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt s7: 'Preferably, a title should not begin with the name "OASIS" except on the recommendation of Project Administration for special cases.' Section 7's lead sentence track-scopes this to BLOCKER (Standards Track, must-observe) / WARN (Non-Standards Track, should-follow with an additional alternate-construction escape valve).

conditions.sig: No Authors section or byline found
conditions.condition: A Technical Report/Technical Report Draft names its Authors on the cover page (heading or title-block byline)
conditions.pulls: a '## Authors'/'## Author(s)' heading (scoped to the front-matter window through Abstract), or a 'by <Name>' title-block byline (scoped to the title/type-label window), on a package whose cover-adjacent type label is Technical Report or Technical Report Draft
conditions.compares_to: TC Handbook, Technical Reports: 'A Technical Report has one or more named Authors ... recorded on the cover page'

conditions.sig: Authors section is empty or placeholder-only
conditions.condition: The Authors heading/byline is not empty or placeholder-only (tbd/n/a/none), including list/task/blockquote-dressed variants
conditions.pulls: each line under the Authors heading (or the byline content), with list/task/blockquote markup and whitespace stripped
conditions.compares_to: at least one non-placeholder named entry must remain

conditions.condition: A Technical Report Draft's Authors section is not left on the registry's own tolerated 'Will be filled in' placeholder indefinitely (WARN while still a TRD)
conditions.pulls: the Authors heading content (or byline content) when it normalizes to exactly the 'will be filled in' placeholder, on a package classified TRD
conditions.compares_to: the existing residue-check precedent (check='residue') tolerating 'Will be filled in' pre-CS, scoped here to the Authors record of an in-progress Technical Report Draft

conditions.sig: still reads 'will be filled in' on an approved Technical Report
conditions.condition: An approved (non-draft) Technical Report's Authors section is resolved, not still the 'Will be filled in' placeholder
conditions.pulls: the Authors heading content (or byline content) on a package classified as the final Technical Report (not TRD)
conditions.compares_to: the TRD-stage 'will be filled in' tolerance does not survive Full Majority Vote approval to the final Technical Report

conditions.sig: must never be used in a filename or directory name that is used in a document URI
conditions.condition: No underscore in an identifying (document-URI-bearing) package name
conditions.pulls: the stage directory name, the version directory name, each stage-root delivery-item filename sharing the package's established basename, and any Multi-Part partN-name directory/file
conditions.compares_to: STRICT allowlist [A-Za-z0-9.-]. Naming Directives v1.7 s3: an UNDERSCORE 'must never be used in a filename or directory name that is used in a document URI'

conditions.sig: no exception applies to an identifying package name
conditions.condition: No character outside the sixty-four permitted characters in an identifying package name
conditions.pulls: the stage directory name, the version directory name, each stage-root delivery-item filename sharing the package's established basename, and any Multi-Part partN-name directory/file
conditions.compares_to: STRICT allowlist [A-Za-z0-9.-]. Naming Directives v1.7 s3: 'TCs must use only the sixty-four characters from among alphanumerics [A-Za-z0-9] and the two punctuation characters ... PERIOD ... and ... HYPHEN'

conditions.sig: no other character is permitted anywhere in the package
conditions.condition: No character outside the sixty-four permitted characters plus UNDERSCORE in a supporting (non-identifying) package name
conditions.pulls: every filename and directory basename in the package tree outside the identifying set
conditions.compares_to: BASE allowlist [A-Za-z0-9._-]. Naming Directives v1.7 s3 base 'must use only' clause, with UNDERSCORE included per the conditional tolerance

conditions.sig: an empty name cannot satisfy it
conditions.condition: An identifying (document-URI-bearing) package name is non-empty
conditions.pulls: the stage directory name, the version directory name, each stage-root delivery-item filename sharing the package's established basename, and any Multi-Part partN-name directory/file
conditions.compares_to: STRICT test ^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$: the '+' quantifier requires at least one character, so an empty identifying name trivially fails the sixty-four-permitted-character allowlist; mirrors how check_stage_name's and check_version_naming's own fullmatch patterns already reject an empty stage/version token without any special-casing

conditions.sig: has no file extension after the document-identifier stem
conditions.condition: A stage-directory-root delivery item (the established document-identifier stem plus one packaged format) carries at least one file extension
conditions.pulls: each delivery-item basename in items, with the 'filenames' check's already-validated shared stem subtracted from the front (only when the basename shares a clean extension boundary with the stem)
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives v1.7 s4: 'A single file(name) extension must be used in each filename except for a recognized set of extensionless filenames in common use.' BLOCKER at published stages, WARN at wd (s5.2 Note: working drafts 'may use any file naming pattern preferred by the TC'); wd-stage match is case-folded.

conditions.sig: carries more than one file extension after the stem
conditions.condition: A stage-directory-root delivery item carries exactly one file extension after the stem (or one blessed compound: tar.gz/tar.bz2/tar.xz, and only when that compound is the WHOLE remaining suffix)
conditions.pulls: each delivery-item basename in items, with the shared stem subtracted from the front, split into trailing dot-segments (an empty segment from a doubled or trailing dot is kept, so a malformed name is still counted)
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives v1.7 s4's single-extension rule, structurally against the same stem boundary the 'filenames' check already validates. BLOCKER at published stages, WARN at wd.

conditions.condition: A non-delivery-item (Tier B) file with zero dots is one of the three literally recognized extensionless names
conditions.pulls: every file basename in the package tree outside the Tier A delivery-item set, junk-files' forbidden names and forbidden directories, and dotfiles
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives v1.7 s9: 'Exceptions to the rule that every filename must include a file extension include: CATALOG or catalog, README, ChangeLog.' Non-blocking WARN per s4's Applicability carve-out for non-identification-pattern files.

conditions.sig: commonly denotes a file extension elsewhere
conditions.condition: A non-delivery-item (Tier B) dotted filename's penultimate segment does not look like a known extension token (or the trailing pair is a blessed compound)
conditions.pulls: every dotted file basename in the package tree outside the Tier A delivery-item set, junk-files' forbidden names and forbidden directories, and dotfiles; its last two dot-segments
conditions.compares_to: A disclosed, non-exhaustive known-extension-token vocabulary (not an IANA-derived classification); flagged only as a non-blocking heuristic pattern-match advisory per s4's Applicability carve-out for non-identification-pattern files (schemas, images, WSDLs, XML/JSON artifacts).

conditions.sig: is not on this check's table of common OASIS publication rendering-format extensions
conditions.condition: Every root principal/stage-identifying filename and every Multi-Part named-part filename uses an extension that matches a common OASIS publication rendering format
conditions.pulls: the file extension token (lowercased, split on the last '.') of every root-level filename that shares the package's known delivery stem, and every filename anywhere in the package whose stem is that same delivery stem plus '-part<N>-<partName>'
conditions.compares_to: a curated allowlist of common OASIS document/publication rendering-format extensions (txt, md, html, htm, pdf, doc, docx, odt, ods, odp, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, rtf, xml, json, epub), per Naming Directives Section 4 'File extensions should conform to industry best practice, matching well-known IANA MIME Media Types'; filenames on the Section 9 extensionless allowlist (CATALOG, catalog, README, ChangeLog) are exempt

conditions.condition: A non-document-identifier artifact's own filename does not embed a stage+revision token
conditions.pulls: the full basename of every package file outside the delivery items, the delivery-stem-plus-recognized-suffix set (multi-part -partN-partName / public-review-metadata / comment-resolution-log, each restricted to the extensions a real prose side-file carries), and package-management files (manifest, checksum manifests, exact README/LICENSE variants, _audit/, OS junk)
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives s4: 'it is considered inadvisable to incorporate instance-specific [stage][revision] data for any release in filenames other than in the document identifier files ... thus mySchema.xsd but NOT mySchema-csd02.xsd'; TCs are advised to use named subdirectories and retain stable/identical filenames per s5.2/5.3's stage-abbreviation and two-digit-revision definitions

conditions.condition: Every Multi-Part Work Product part filename embeds the identical WP-abbrev token
conditions.pulls: the WP-abbrev token from every stage-root and part-subdirectory filename matching the Multi-Part Naming Directives grammar (<WP-abbrev>-<version-id>-<stage-abbrev><rev>-part<N>-<partName>)
conditions.compares_to: the set of distinct WP-abbrev tokens across all matched part filenames must collapse to exactly one value, per TC Process 2.2.3's single Work Product name and the Handbook's Multi-part work products restatement

conditions.condition: Every Multi-Part Work Product part filename embeds the identical version-id token
conditions.pulls: the version-id token from every stage-root and part-subdirectory filename matching the Multi-Part Naming Directives grammar (<WP-abbrev>-<version-id>-<stage-abbrev><rev>-part<N>-<partName>)
conditions.compares_to: the set of distinct version-id tokens across all matched part filenames must collapse to exactly one value, per TC Process 2.2.3's single Work Product version number and the Handbook's Multi-part work products restatement

conditions.sig: bare canonical filename in a multi-part package
conditions.condition: No bare CORE.ext delivery filename coexists with genuine part files
conditions.pulls: delivery-item stems sharing one <wp>-<version>-<stage> core, and their tails
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt s4: the single-part bare-CORE filename rule does not apply once the package is multi-part

conditions.condition: Every non-canonical delivery filename sharing the package core carries a well-formed -part<N>-<name> segment
conditions.pulls: the tail (text after the resolved <wp>-<version>-<stage> core) of each in-scope delivery filename
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives v1.7 s4 multi-part filename grammar: literal lowercase 'part' + Arabic numeral + hyphen + partName, positioned before the extension

conditions.sig: part filename and containing part-directory disagree
conditions.condition: A part file discovered inside an Option-1 URI part-subdirectory agrees with that subdirectory's own [partNumber]-[partName] segment
conditions.pulls: the part number/name parsed from the filename tail and from its containing part-subdirectory name
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt s6.1 (Option 1): the subdirectory segment and the filename's part identifier must name the same part

conditions.sig: part number reused for different parts
conditions.condition: Each part number maps to exactly one partName across every format variant and discovery location
conditions.pulls: the (number, partName) pairs extracted from every in-scope filename tail
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives v1.7 s4: partNumber identifies one distinct separately-titled prose part, not two

conditions.sig: part numbering does not begin at 1
conditions.condition: Part numbering for a multi-part package begins at 1
conditions.pulls: the sorted set of unique part numbers found across the package's in-scope delivery filenames
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt s4: partNumber begins with the number '1' (for Part 1)

conditions.sig: part numbering is not monotonically increasing / contains a gap
conditions.condition: Part numbering for a multi-part package is contiguous with no gaps
conditions.pulls: the sorted set of unique part numbers found across the package's in-scope delivery filenames
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt s4: partNumber increases monotonically (2, 3, 4, ...) for other parts, i.e. the exact sequence [1, 2, ..., N]

conditions.sig: does not carry the required companion file
conditions.condition: A live, published csd/cnd stage directory confirmed (by tiered evidence) and successfully scanned to have undergone TC public review carries the required public-review-metadata companion file
conditions.pulls: the LIVE docs.oasis-open.org stage-directory-root filename listing (fetched over the network, post-publication audit only), plus a same-revision comment-resolution-log or a downstream cs/errata stage's own Previous-stage cover URL as evidence the review occurred
conditions.compares_to: the exact, case-sensitive filename [WP-abbrev]-[version-id]-[stage-abbrev][revisionNumber]-public-review-metadata.html (naming-directives.txt 5.2; handbook-Naming.txt 'Public-review metadata filename (new in v1.7)')

conditions.condition: A present public-review-metadata companion file is non-empty
conditions.pulls: the byte length of the fetched companion file
conditions.compares_to: naming-directives.txt 5.2: the file 'provides a publication history of the Work Product' (content validation itself is out of scope for this check; only non-zero size is tested here)

conditions.sig: could not be fetched to confirm its content
conditions.condition: A public-review-metadata companion file listed in the live directory is actually reachable so its content can be evaluated
conditions.pulls: the HTTP status of a direct fetch of the listed companion filename
conditions.compares_to: a listing entry alone is not proof of a readable file; an unreachable listed file stays an open advisory rather than a silent, unreviewed pass

conditions.sig: resembling the required comment-resolution-log is present but misnamed
conditions.condition: A file resembling a comment-resolution-log, if present in a CSD/CND stage directory that itself carries a public-review-metadata file, carries the exact basename Naming Directives prescribes
conditions.pulls: the sibling file listing of the stage directory root (immediate siblings of the document-identifier files only, per naming-directives.txt's 'directory with the CSD or CND' scoping); whether any sibling basename (extension stripped, hyphen/underscore-normalized) contains 'commentresolutionlog' without exactly matching the expected basename under a plausible-format extension
conditions.compares_to: the expected basename [stem]-comment-resolution-log against naming-directives.txt s5.2's filename pattern for a produced comment resolution log

conditions.condition: Where in-package evidence (a later-stage sibling directory) shows a CSD/CND public review has demonstrably concluded, a comment-resolution-log basename match was sought and not found
conditions.pulls: the sibling file listing of the stage directory root; the presence of a later-stage sibling directory (cs/os/errata for a csd gate, cn for a cnd gate) alongside this stage directory, as the review-concluded closure signal
conditions.compares_to: tc-process.txt s2.6/s2.7 (comment disposition is required to be posted to the TC's e-mail lists; the downstream approval ballot may only commence once every comment is resolved) against handbook-PublicReviews.txt's 'best practice, not a normative filing mandate' framing for HOW that record is kept

conditions.sig: normative-definition file is never referenced from the Work Product
conditions.condition: Every candidate normative-definition file (schema/grammar/code plain-text file, excluding example/sample/test-case/non-normative and pipeline/asset directories) is referenced from the Work Product
conditions.pulls: each candidate file's package-relative path and basename, tested via structured link/href/src/schemaLocation/$ref target extraction (path-level, then basename-level) against the spec's own text (or rendered HTML on the DOCX track), every OTHER candidate file's own content and extracted targets, and manifest.json (package root only)/top-level README-or-index text, all normalized (URL-decode, Unicode NFC)
conditions.compares_to: TC Process 2.2.5: 'Each text file must be referenced from the Work Product; and'. Standards Track (csd, cs, os, errata) only

conditions.sig: basename-only reference cannot be unambiguously resolved
conditions.condition: A basename-only match among candidate files sharing that basename in different directories is flagged for confirmation rather than silently satisfying the requirement for every tied file
conditions.pulls: candidate files sharing an identical basename in different package directories, and whether any reference to that basename in the corpus is path-qualified
conditions.compares_to: TC Process 2.2.5's reference requirement; an ambiguous basename-only match does not unambiguously resolve which file was referenced

conditions.condition: No live META-refresh element in any delivered HTML file
conditions.pulls: every <meta> tag in each .html/.htm/.xhtml file, HTML-tokenized (comments/<script>/<style>/<pre>/<code>/<template> excluded)
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives v1.7 s6.5(a): unauthorized URI aliasing via META-refresh elements is barred

conditions.condition: No stage-root delivery file or manifest-cited file (by exact package-relative path) shares byte-identical content with another package-relative path
conditions.pulls: sha256 of every regular file (symlinks resolved to their in-package target's bytes) in the stage/revision directory
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives v1.7 s6.5(b): preparing files with identical content under two different filenames within a published instance is barred

conditions.sig: none of which is a delivery/manifest-cited file
conditions.condition: An ancillary (non-delivery, non-manifest-cited) duplicate is flagged for review, not treated as a s6.5(b) aliasing risk
conditions.pulls: sha256 buckets whose members are all non-citable paths (LICENSE/NOTICE/schemas/test-fixtures/asset directories/etc.)
conditions.compares_to: the package's own delivery-item paths and manifest.json authoritative/delivery-role paths

conditions.condition: The markdown Previous-stage block cites no redirect/URL-shortening domain
conditions.pulls: every URL under the 'Previous Stage/Version' heading
conditions.compares_to: the seed redirect-service domain list (tinyurl.com, bit.ly, goo.gl, ow.ly, t.co, is.gd, buff.ly, rebrand.ly, tiny.cc, cutt.ly, shorturl.at, rb.gy, purl.oclc.org)

conditions.sig: DOCX-native cover field cites a redirect
conditions.condition: The DOCX-native rendered cover's This/Previous/Latest-version fields cite no redirect/URL-shortening domain
conditions.pulls: every URL (visible text or href) between the This/Previous/Latest-version labels on the rendered HTML cover
conditions.compares_to: the seed redirect-service domain list

conditions.sig: names oasis-open.org but links to a redirect
conditions.condition: Plain-prose anchor text that names oasis-open.org does not link to a redirect/URL-shortening domain (markdown source)
conditions.pulls: the visible/anchor text of every `[shown](target)` (md) or `shown` (html) construct whose shown text is not itself a URL (a shown-is-a-URL mismatch is the existing link-mismatch check's territory)
conditions.compares_to: the seed redirect-service domain list, gated on the anchor text literally containing 'oasis-open.org'

conditions.sig: names oasis-open.org but links to a redirect
conditions.condition: Plain-prose anchor text that names oasis-open.org does not link to a redirect/URL-shortening domain (HTML render)
conditions.pulls: the visible/anchor text of every `[shown](target)` (md) or `shown` (html) construct whose shown text is not itself a URL (a shown-is-a-URL mismatch is the existing link-mismatch check's territory)
conditions.compares_to: the seed redirect-service domain list, gated on the anchor text literally containing 'oasis-open.org'

conditions.sig: cites oasis-open.org while linking a redirect
conditions.condition: A bare URL's enclosing sentence that names oasis-open.org does not point at a redirect/URL-shortening domain (markdown source)
conditions.pulls: the sentence-bounded prose window (nearest sentence terminator or paragraph break either side) around every bare URL not part of a link construct
conditions.compares_to: the seed redirect-service domain list, gated on the sentence window literally containing 'oasis-open.org'

conditions.sig: cites oasis-open.org while linking a redirect
conditions.condition: A bare URL's enclosing sentence that names oasis-open.org does not point at a redirect/URL-shortening domain (HTML render)
conditions.pulls: the sentence-bounded prose window (nearest sentence terminator or paragraph break either side) around every bare URL not part of a link construct
conditions.compares_to: the seed redirect-service domain list, gated on the sentence window literally containing 'oasis-open.org'

conditions.condition: An http(s) namespace's tail matches the docs.oasis-open.org/[tc-shortname]/ns/xxxx pattern
conditions.pulls: targetNamespace on the root of each packaged .xsd/.wsdl (incl. wsdl:types-embedded schemas), and the ns attribute on the root grammar/element of each .rng
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives s8 pattern http(s)://docs.oasis-open.org/[tc-shortname]/ns/xxxx, xxxx restricted to the s3 sixty-four-character set plus internal '/', terminating in '/', '#', or alphanumeric; BLOCKER when the tc-shortname has no pattern-grandfather allowlist entry

conditions.condition: A pattern-mismatched namespace's tc-shortname is a confirmed-approved pre-2012 pattern grandfather
conditions.pulls: the same pattern-mismatched namespace URI, matched against the pattern-grandfather allowlist
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives v1.2 s9: pre-2012 practice 'may be grandfathered, if approved by Project Administration': WARN when listed but approval is not machine-confirmable at check time

conditions.sig: declared under both http and https scheme
conditions.condition: The same namespace tail is declared under one scheme only, package-wide
conditions.pulls: every http(s) namespace URI declared by any packaged .xsd/.wsdl(+embedded)/.rng in the package, grouped by scheme-stripped tail
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives s8: 'While either "http" or "https" may be used ... they are not interchangeable. One or the other must be used consistently.'

conditions.condition: A urn:-scheme declared namespace's TC is on the URN-grandfather allowlist
conditions.pulls: the urn:-scheme namespace URI and its owning tc-shortname
conditions.compares_to: Naming Directives s8: URN-based namespaces 'must not be declared otherwise', permitted only for TCs that already used the feature (or Maintenance Activity TCs), approved by Project Administration

conditions.sig: not evaluated by this check -- manual review
conditions.condition: A RELAX NG grammar declares only one namespace, on its root grammar/element node
conditions.pulls: every ns attribute on non-root nodes of a .rng file, compared to the root node's ns
conditions.compares_to: this check only validates the root-level self-declared namespace; a differing non-root ns is flagged for manual review rather than silently dropped

conditions.condition: This-stage and Latest-stage cover URIs do not reuse the reserved /ns/ path segment
conditions.pulls: the This-stage and Latest-stage URL(s) from the markdown front matter (md track) or the rendered HTML cover (docx-native track, via the shared html_cover_urls() helper)
conditions.compares_to: handbook-Naming.txt: '/ns/ ... is for namespace identifiers, not for retrievable documents. Do not use /ns/ in the URI of a document you intend to publish as a retrievable resource'

conditions.condition: Previous-stage cover URI does not reuse the reserved /ns/ path segment (non-blocking, manual-review if it does: an immutable inherited citation)
conditions.pulls: the Previous-stage URL from the markdown front matter (md track) or the rendered HTML cover (docx-native track, via the shared html_cover_urls() helper)
conditions.compares_to: handbook-Naming.txt's /ns/ reservation rule, applied to an already-published prior-stage citation the current package cannot alter

stage-token.result: PASS -- Previous-stage tokens match/legacy-clean or N/A, Latest-stage filenames carry no stage token

template.sections_found: Abstract, Chair(s), Citation format, Editor(s), Latest stage/version, Notices, Previous stage/version, Status, Technical Committee / Open Project, This stage/version
